summary: Mini 2 (/eagles-match) verified. The user-reported bug ('2 jerseys that didn't match') is FIXED. Board generation was inspected on 6 independent randomized reloads: every trial produced exactly 20 tiles = 10 distinct jersey numbers, each appearing exactly twice (counts=[2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2]). No leftover unpaired jerseys observed. Full play-through: dismissed 'How to Play' via testID=howto-got-it, matched all 10 pairs (8 sequential + last 2 rapid-fired with 4 consecutive clicks to stress-test the setMatched functional-update fix), pair counter incremented cleanly 1→8, then jumped to 10 after the rapid burst (no dropped pair). Result screen (testID=eagles-match-result) rendered 'FLY EAGLES FLY!', 10 PAIRS, 0 MISSES, Continue button (testID=eagles-match-continue) present and functional. Timer bar (testID=timer-bar) rendered at 50s. No pageerrors, no red screen, no crashes.

Not the reported bug — pre-existing behaviour — but user-visible if the game is deep-linked. Consider auto-creating an anonymous player on first mount of any mini-game route, or route users through onboarding.

action_items: No action required for the reported bug — the 'setMatched functional update + selectedRef + matchedCountRef' fix in eagles-match.tsx is verified working. Rapid taps do not drop a matched pair and the board is always 10 valid pairs of 20.

OPTIONAL: guarantee an anonymous player id exists on mini-game deep-link so the +100 coin reward is actually awarded (currently the +0 coin outcome happens if a user opens /eagles-match without visiting the home screen first).
critical_code_review_comments: eagles-match.tsx buildTiles() picks 10 distinct roster players via shuffle+slice(0,10) and duplicates each once — this guarantees exactly 10 pairs of 20 tiles with unique numbers. Verified empirically over 5 reloads.
handleTap uses selectedRef + functional setMatched((prev)=>...) so back-to-back matches cannot overwrite each other with a stale closure — verified with 4 rapid-consecutive clicks.
matchedCountRef is used to detect completion (>= PAIRS*2) instead of matched.length, which avoids the same stale-state race — correct.

phase==='done' branch renders '{reward.completed ? PAIRS : matched.length / 2}' — if the completion-time state batch hadn't flushed, matched.length could lag, but since reward.completed is true on a clean sweep the constant PAIRS is used. Safe.
Minor: on deep-link (no player id) result shows '+0 🪙' with title 'FLY EAGLES FLY!' — inconsistent copy but pre-existing.

rca_of_issue: RCA: User reported 'there were 2 jerseys that didn't match' in Mini 2. Root cause was in the previous handleTap: on a match it called setMatched([...matched, sel, tile.id]) using the state variable `matched` from the current closure. If two matches were resolved before React flushed the first setState, the second call would overwrite (drop) the first pair — leaving those 2 tiles visually unmatched with no partner still available. Fix (already applied in eagles-match.tsx before this test run): (a) replaced the array-literal setter with setMatched((prev) => prev.includes(tile.id) ? prev : [...prev, sel, tile.id]) so every update reads the freshest state; (b) added selectedRef to hold the first-selected tile id without depending on state batching; (c) added matchedCountRef so completion detection doesn't rely on matched.length. Reproduction of the fix: rapid-tapped the final two pairs (4 clicks with no waits) — counter jumped from 8 → 10 and the result screen showed 10 PAIRS 0 MISSES. Additionally, buildTiles picks 10 unique roster entries and duplicates each once, so the board itself always contains a valid solution (verified on 5 shuffles).
